title: KEDA percentile smoothing caused gradual-ramp underprovisioning and cold-start cascade
creator: Erin Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-26 we observed a gradual traffic ramp across several customer routes that resulted in sustained elevation of 95th-percentile per-instance request rate. Instead of triggering smooth scale-up, the KEDA scaler's percentile-based smoothing window suppressed intermediate metric signals and delayed scaler reactions. This led to sequential underprovisioning across pods, a cascade of cold-starts when new replicas finally came up, and increased tail latency for ~45 minutes. Impact: multiple mid-size customers using Dedicated pools reported intermittent timeouts and latency spikes (P50 within bounds but P95 and P99 degraded). No data loss or security exposure. Postmortem assembled by Erin Patel; triage and mitigation led by Luca Moreno.
impact: Approx 45 minutes of elevated P95/P99 latency for 7 impacted customer routes across two Dedicated clusters. Increased token cost due to retry storms; SLO blips recorded in console dashboards. Customers notified via status.redwood.ai and follow-up emails from customer success.
timeline: 2026-02-26 09:10 UTC - Canary alert: slow ramp detected on canary route; increased 95p request rate observed in telemetry.
2026-02-26 09:16 UTC - Ops page triggered; initial mitigation attempted by increasing HPA maxReplicas in cluster A (manual override).
2026-02-26 09:30 UTC - KEDA scaler failed to scale proportionally due to percentile smoothing; metrics dashboard showed smoothed 95p remaining below threshold despite rising instantaneous load.
2026-02-26 09:45 UTC - Cold-start cascade: multiple pods registered as NotReady during image pull/start; queueing increased latency further.
2026-02-26 10:00 UTC - Emergency rollback: switched scaling policy to a temporary CPU-based HPA for affected deployments; latency improved gradually.
2026-02-26 10:55 UTC - Full mitigation: pre-warm warm-pool instances and set HPA minReplicas=2 for the impacted service. Incident declared resolved at 10:55 UTC.
2026-03-01 - Postmortem review meeting; agreed on action items and owners.
2026-03-08 - KEDA metric exporter patch merged to expose raw percentiles and instantaneous rates (PR #3896).
2026-03-12 - Canary e2e test added to chaos suite; bounding tests for percentile window behavior applied (release runtime-1.23).
root_cause: Combination of a percentile-based smoothing implementation in our KEDA scaler and a long smoothing window meant to suppress noisy spikes. During a gradual ramp, this smoothing hid sustained increases in instantaneous request rate; the scaler did not assertively scale until threshold was exceeded for the smoothed metric. When pods eventually launched, image pull times + startup hooks created cold starts that amplified queueing.
contributing_factors: Percentile smoothing window configured to 10 minutes for 95th percentile metric - too long for gradual ramps
KEDA scaler used a smoothed percentile value rather than delta or instantaneous request rate for scale decisions
No predictive/pre-warm scaling policy or warm-pool configured for these routes
Image startup time variance not modeled in readiness gating (heavy model artifacts for some tenants)
Lack of an alert that correlates instantaneous rate slope with smoothed percentile divergence
mitigations: Immediate: manual HPA override to CPU-based scaling for impacted services (2026-02-26)
Short-term: added HPA minReplicas=2 and enabled warm-pool pre-warm for Dedicated cluster A (2026-02-26)
Medium-term: patched KEDA metric exporter to expose both raw instantaneous rate and percentile summaries (PR #3896 merged 2026-03-08)
Long-term: implement predictive scaling policy using traffic forecasts from request router and add pre-warming for scheduled ramps
action_items: Luca Moreno - 2026-03-19 - Reduce 95p smoothing window from 10m to 60s for request-rate scaler profiles and roll out to staging clusters; validate with canary ramps
Sana Kim - 2026-03-22 - Add an HPA/KEDA compatibility test in chaos-suite that asserts scaler reacts to instantaneous-rate slope increases (test id: chaos-autoscale-014)
Diego Alvarez - 2026-03-25 - Implement a new KEDA scaler mode that uses a hybrid signal (instantaneous rate + short percentile) and add config flag 'hybrid_signal_v1'
Erin Patel - 2026-03-26 - Create runbook for manual override to CPU-based HPA and warm-pool activation; include step-by-step in on-call handbook
Platform Ops - 2026-04-02 - Inventory image startup tails and publish per-service startup percentiles; add to deployment metadata for autoscaling decisions
Customer Success - 2026-03-20 - Follow-up customer communication template and RCA summary for affected tenants
postmortem_notes: This incident highlights the trade-off between noise suppression and responsiveness in percentile-based scalers. Our initial decision to use long smoothing windows reduced noise but increased time-to-scale for sustained ramps.
When updating scaling algorithms, ensure we have canary traffic patterns that mirror gradual customer ramps (not only step-load tests).
Consider shipping scaler config changes behind a feature flag and gating with per-cluster canaries.
Assign a follow-up review in 30 days to validate that hybrid_signal_v1 doesn't regress on noisy workloads.
